acad.description: Rocky headlands and coastal islands on Mount Desert Island, with Cadillac Mountain sunrise views, carriage roads, and tidepool beaches.

arch.description: Over 2,000 natural sandstone arches plus balanced rocks and fins near Moab, sculpted from Entrada Sandstone.

badl.description: Eroded buttes, pinnacles and prairie grasslands in southwestern South Dakota, rich with Oligocene fossils and bison.

bibe.description: Desert, mountains and the Rio Grande in remote west Texas; contains the entire Chisos Basin and a bend in the river.

bisc.description: Aquatic park protecting Biscayne Bay, coral reefs, mangrove shorelines and the northernmost Florida Keys.

blca.fullName: Black Canyon of the Gunnison National Park
blca.description: Steep, dark, narrow gorge carved by the Gunnison River through hard metamorphic rock in western Colorado.

brca.description: Natural amphitheaters of hoodoos (spire-like rock formations) at high elevation on the Paunsaugunt Plateau.

cany.description: Colorado Plateau canyons carved by the Green and Colorado rivers near Moab, divided into Island in the Sky, Needles and Maze districts.

care.description: Waterpocket Fold monocline with white domes, red rocks and historic orchards in south-central Utah.

crla.description: Deepest lake in the United States, formed in the caldera of Mount Mazama, known for its intense blue color and Rim Drive.

dena.description: Six million acres of Alaskan wilderness centered on Denali (20,310 ft), the highest peak in North America.

deva.description: Hottest, driest and lowest national park, with below-sea-level basins, salt flats, dunes and colorful badlands.

ever.description: Vast subtropical wetland of slow-moving river of grass, mangroves and sawgrass prairies, habitat for alligators and manatees.

gaar.fullName: Gates of the Arctic National Park and Preserve
gaar.description: Roadless wilderness in the Brooks Range above the Arctic Circle, with glaciated valleys and wild rivers.

glba.fullName: Glacier Bay National Park and Preserve
glba.description: Tidewater glaciers, fjords and temperate rainforest in southeastern Alaska, accessible mostly by boat or plane.

glac.description: Crown of the Continent with glaciated peaks, alpine lakes and Going-to-the-Sun Road along the Continental Divide.

grba.description: Diverse park in eastern Nevada with Wheeler Peak, ancient bristlecone pines, Lehman Caves and some of the darkest night skies.

grsa.fullName: Great Sand Dunes National Park and Preserve
grsa.description: Tallest dunes in North America against the Sangre de Cristo Mountains, with seasonal Medano Creek.

grsm.description: Ridge upon ridge of forested Appalachian mountains on the Tennessee-North Carolina border, the most visited national park.

guis.description: Barrier islands with white sand beaches, coastal forts and maritime forests along the Gulf of Mexico.

hale.description: Shield volcano on Maui rising 10,023 ft, with a dramatic summit crater, native Hawaiian ecosystems and the Pools of Oheo.

havo.description: Active volcanism on the Big Island featuring Kilauea and Mauna Loa, lava tubes and recent lava flows.

hot.description: Thermal springs in the Ouachita Mountains of central Arkansas, with historic Bathhouse Row and surrounding forest.

isro.description: Roadless island archipelago in Lake Superior, a wilderness of boreal forest known for moose and wolf populations.

jotr.description: Where the Mojave and Colorado deserts meet, named for the Joshua tree forests with bouldered rock piles and dark skies.

lavo.description: Volcanic landscape in northern California with Lassen Peak, fumaroles, mud pots and all four types of volcanoes.

maca.description: World's longest known cave system with over 400 mapped miles of passages in south-central Kentucky.

meve.description: Ancestral Puebloan cliff dwellings and archaeological sites on a high mesa in southwestern Colorado.

mora.description: 14,410 ft glaciated stratovolcano with subalpine wildflower meadows and old-growth forests in the Cascade Range.

noca.description: Rugged glaciated peaks of the North Cascades with over 300 glaciers and dense conifer forests in northern Washington.

olym.description: Three ecosystems in one park: Pacific coast, temperate rainforest and glaciated Olympic Mountains in northwestern Washington.

pefo.description: Painted Desert and petrified wood from the Late Triassic in northeastern Arizona along historic Route 66.

redw.description: Towering coast redwoods, the tallest trees on Earth, with prairies, rivers and Pacific coastline in northern California.

romo.description: Alpine peaks, Trail Ridge Road and alpine lakes along the Continental Divide in northern Colorado.

seki.fullName: Sequoia and Kings Canyon National Parks
seki.description: Giant sequoia groves including General Sherman, plus deep glacial canyons and high Sierra peaks.

shen.description: Narrow band of Blue Ridge Mountains with Skyline Drive and the Appalachian Trail in Virginia.

thro.description: Badlands of the Little Missouri River in North Dakota, with bison, wild horses and a petrified forest.

viis.description: Tropical forest, coral reefs and historic ruins on two-thirds of Saint John in the U.S. Virgin Islands.

voya.description: Interconnected waterways along the Minnesota-Ontario border, a park best explored by boat with rocky islands and boreal forest.

wind.description: Boxwork-formatted limestone cave and mixed-grass prairie above ground with bison and elk in the Black Hills.

wrst.fullName: Wrangell-St. Elias National Park and Preserve
wrst.description: Largest national park in the U.S. with vast mountain ranges, glaciers and the historic Kennecott copper mines.

yose.description: Granite cliffs of El Capitan and Half Dome, Yosemite Falls, giant sequoias and the glacier-carved Yosemite Valley.

grca.description: A mile-deep canyon carved by the Colorado River across northern Arizona, with South and North rims.

yell.description: World's first national park, with geysers like Old Faithful, hot springs, wildlife and the Grand Canyon of the Yellowstone.

zion.description: Towering sandstone cliffs and slot canyons along the Virgin River in southwestern Utah, including Angels Landing and The Narrows.

grte.description: Rugged Teton Range rising from Jackson Hole with alpine lakes, the Snake River and historic Mormon Row.
